value.body: A science degree in human nutrition: food science, nutritional biochemistry, physiology, diet planning, therapeutic (clinical) nutrition, community nutrition and food-service management. It leads to dietitian and nutritionist work, food-industry quality and research roles, public-health nutrition programmes and postgraduate study. Some universities offer it as a separate major; others as a specialisation within Home Science.

items.label: Course length
items.note: 4 years for Honours / Honours with Research under the UGC four-year UG framework (NEP 2020); some include a hospital internship

items.note: Indian Dietetic Association exam after a degree, a PG qualification and a supervised internship (as reported)

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Class 12, usually in the science stream with Biology or Chemistry; some colleges also accept other streams (rules vary). Central universities admit through CUET-UG scores; many state universities and their colleges admit on Class 12 merit or a state test. Agricultural universities that offer B.Sc (Hons) Food, Nutrition & Dietetics or Community Science admit through ICAR's quota (via CUET-UG) or a state entrance.

value.title: At a glance
items: Hospital dietitian posts usually expect a PG diploma or M.Sc, an internship, or the RD credential — the B.Sc alone is often a starting point.
Food companies, wellness and fitness firms, and public-health nutrition programmes also hire nutrition graduates.
Common next steps are an M.Sc in Food & Nutrition or Dietetics, a PG diploma in dietetics, or an MPH.
